definition: Natural Language Understanding, to understand the relationship and meaning in text data.
details: Natural Language Understanding, to understand the relationship and meaning in text data.

explainer.lead: NLU, or Natural Language Understanding, is about understanding the relationships and meaning in text data. It matters because extracting meaning, not just words, is what lets systems respond to what text actually says.

tiers.eli5: It's the part of a computer system that tries to actually understand what words mean, not just spot them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply NLU to derive relationships and meaning from text rather than surface tokens alone. A pitfall is treating word matching as understanding, when the task is the meaning and relations behind the text.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as understanding the relationship and meaning in text data; no formula or bound is specified.

explainer.example: Given text mentioning two people and an action between them, an NLU system would aim to capture that relationship rather than only the individual words.
